messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · INC-31415 · Severity: SEV2 · detected sudden KV prefix cache cardinality growth + continuous-batching regression in us-west. Trigger: 5xx spike, OOM on worker-03. Pager: @ashwin. Link: <https://pager.example/INC-31415>

ashwin: on it, joining voice in ~2m. quick summary: spike in tail latency and token throughput dropped. seeing OOMs on a few kv-serving workers.

jules: saw a huge increase in unique prefix keys — looks like prefetch exploded. mem usage on kv-worker-03 jumped ~4x in 6 minutes.

leila: any customer-facing 5xx/timeouts? severity assessment?

maria: support chiming in — ACME and two smaller customers reported intermittent timeouts and 504s. no PII or exfil reports. tickets opened.

ashwin: first mitigation: reduce batching window and disable prefix prefetch to stop the prefetch storms. preparing a hotfix to config-store. will do rolling apply to us-west.

jules: proposed config change:
```
continuous_batch.max_window_ms=5
continuous_batch.max_tokens=1024
kv.prefix_prefetch.enabled=false
```
I'll push to canary first.

maria: notifying AE/team for affected accounts now.

oncall-bot: ashwin accepted the incident. change window set to 10m for handoff.

samir: also recommend setting aggressive TTL/eviction for prefix cache while we triage:
```
kv.prefix_cache.max_entries=200000
kv.prefix_cache.ttl_sec=900
```
That should trim runaway entries.

leila: rolling the config to 3 nodes in us-west now. watching mem and 5xx. p95 latency currently 2.3s.

ashwin: deploying patch (snippet):
```bash
# apply config patch to us-west clusters
redwoodctl config set --cluster us-west continuous_batch.max_window_ms 5
redwoodctl config set --cluster us-west kv.prefix_prefetch.enabled false
redwoodctl rollout restart deployment/kv-worker -n redwood-us-west --max-unavailable=1
```
I'll monitor metrics and logs.

jules: logs showing the OOM sequence:
```
[2026-06-15T14:22:11Z] worker-03 kernel: Out of memory: killing process 27122 (kv-worker)
[2026-06-15T14:22:12Z] worker-03 systemd: kv-worker.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/ KILL
[2026-06-15T14:24:05Z] worker-03 kv-worker: started, mem usage steady
```

maria: support report: ACME saw ~27 failed requests during the peak window, all returned 504s. They've been informed and we promised a post-incident summary.

ashwin: initial metrics after config change: prefix cache cardinality dropped from ~12M to ~1.1M after TTL eviction kicked in. continuous_batch queue length reduced. 5xx count falling.

leila: digging into root cause — found a recent rollout to the template-renderer service that changed trimming behavior for templates (preserved trailing whitespace). That caused prompt/tokenizer output to differ subtly, which changed prompt hash prefixes. Hash churn => cache churn => prefetch storms and massive cardinality growth. Also backpressure increased batching windows leading to larger payloads. Chain: tokenizer drift -> hash churn -> prefetch + bigger batches -> KV mem growth.

jules: confirmed. the tokenizer differences changed token boundaries for many templates so old stable keys started missing and prefetch attempted to warm new keys in bulk.

ashwin: mitigation plan: 1) revert prefetch + reduce batch window (done) 2) add fallback deterministic hashing to map v2->v1 keys for a grace period 3) patch template renderer to normalize whitespace and tokenization to previous behavior 4) add prefetch rate limiter and cardinality alarms.

jules: PR prepared: normalize_template_rendering (strip trailing spaces) + hash_fallback_table. Will cherry-pick to canary branch and ship after smoke tests.

maria: support update: ACME now reporting service recovered; they saw errors only during the ~14:22-14:31 window. No data loss. SLA exposure: borderline for that tenant, logging for crediting if needed.

support-bot: created customer note and opened INC-31415-customer-summary.

ashwin: canary rollout in us-west passed at 14:40 (10m monitoring). will continue to roll forward to remaining nodes in the region. rollback plan ready if any 5xx spike observed.

leila: p95 latency down ~35%, 5xx counts near zero. No further OOMs observed.

samir: creating follow-up ticket INF-5678: implement prompt-hash drift detection, prefetch rate limiter, automated TTL scaling and safer hash migration tooling. Assign to eng-ml and eng-runtime.

jules: I'll own the postmortem write-up with timeline, root cause, and action items.

ashwin: handing incident to jules for follow-up & postmortem. I'll be available for 1 hour for questions. :thumbsup:

jules: taking ownership. immediate action items: 1) ship template normalization hotfix 2) add hash fallback mapping for 2 weeks 3) tune prefetch rate limiter 4) add alert for prefix cardinality delta > 1M in 5m.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-31415 RESOLVED by ashwin, jules, leila, samir. Auto-close in 24h if no regression.

maria: adding internal customer comms and summary. will attach to postmortem.

jules: postmortem link (draft): <https://confluence.example/INC-31415-postmortem> — will publish once reviewed.

ashwin: ty everyone for quick turn. biggest takeaway: tokenizer/template changes must include backward-compatible hash migration plan and stronger prefetch safeguards.

maria: echo — support follow-up will coordinate credits and customer notes.

leila: leaving a note to add unit tests for template normalization and tokenization parity.

support-bot: closing customer-facing ticket for ACME; will append final credit details after postmortem.

jules: will file RFC for hash migration workflow next sprint.

ashwin: handing off — i'm out of rotation for now.

support-bot: Incident log saved.

jules: closing thread; follow-ups tracked in INF-5678 and the postmortem.
